keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «채륜이 가볍고 매끄러워 글쓰기 쉬운 종이를 만들었다(발명)» 와 «채륜의 단순한 발명이 지식을 온 세상에 퍼뜨렸다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the invention (Cai Lun made paper that was light, smooth, and easy to write on) and the conclusion (his simple invention helped knowledge spread to the whole world). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: How Cai Lun’s paper changed the world

boxes.qen: How did Cai Lun make paper?
boxes.a: He mashed bark, cloth, and old nets in water
Books became cheap, and knowledge spread

words: The emperor's records were written on heavy bamboo strips
written information kept for the future

qs.q: Why did Cai Lun want something light and cheap?
qs.qko: 채륜이 가볍고 값싼 것을 원한 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Because records were written on heavy bamboo strips or on very expensive silk
Because the emperor wanted books made from wood
Because fishing nets were too heavy to carry
evs: The emperor's records were written on heavy bamboo strips or on silk, which was very expensive.
He mashed tree bark, old cloth, and even worn-out fishing nets in water.
Paper made from wood became common only in the 1800s.
Cai Lun's simple invention helped knowledge spread to the whole world.
why: 황제의 기록이 무거운 대나무 조각이나 아주 비싼 비단에 쓰였기 때문이라고 했어요.
The emperor's records were written on heavy bamboo strips or on silk, which was very expensive.

qs.q: In "even worn-out fishing nets," what does "worn-out" mean?
qs.qko: «even worn-out fishing nets» 에서 «worn-out» 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: old and damaged from long use
evs: He mashed tree bark, old cloth, and even worn-out fishing nets in water.
Cai Lun wanted something light and cheap.
The result was paper that was light, smooth, and easy to write on.
Paper slowly traveled from China to Korea, Japan, the Middle East, and Europe, and books became cheap enough for ordinary people.
why: 그물을 «old cloth(헌 옷감)» 와 함께 물에 짓이겼다고 했으니, «worn-out» 은 오래 써서 낡았다는 뜻이에요.
The nets are mashed together with «old cloth», so «worn-out» means old and damaged from long use.

qs.q: How did Cai Lun turn bark and old nets into paper?
qs.qko: 채륜은 나무껍질과 낡은 그물을 어떻게 종이로 바꾸었나요?
opts: He mashed them in water, then spread the mixture thin, pressed it, and dried it
He burned them and mixed the ash with silk
He cut them into thin strips like bamboo
evs: He mashed tree bark, old cloth, and even worn-out fishing nets in water.
People used rags and plants, and Koreans made strong hanji from mulberry bark.
Then he spread the mixture thin, pressed it flat, and let it dry in the sun.
Paper slowly traveled from China to Korea, Japan, the Middle East, and Europe, and books became cheap enough for ordinary people.
why: 먼저 나무껍질, 헌 옷감, 낡은 그물을 물에 짓이기고, 그다음 얇게 펴서 납작하게 누른 뒤 햇볕에 말렸어요. 두 문장을 이어야 과정이 보여요.
First he mashed bark, cloth, and old nets in water, then he spread the mixture thin, pressed it flat, and dried it in the sun. You need both sentences.

ends: How do people make Korean hanji from mulberry bark?
How did Korea print one of the oldest books with metal type?
세계에서 가장 오래된 금속 활자 책, 직지는 어떻게 만들었을까요?

write.src: “It is important to <u>share good books</u> because <u>they help knowledge spread</u>.”
write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «중요한 일 + 그 이유» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write something important and the reason in English.
write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을» 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because books became cheap for everyone)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «because», write who + what to make your reason clear. (e.g. because books became cheap for everyone)
